answer: A protocol assigns scarce review tasks to identities, not volunteers. Each epoch a seeded shuffle picks K reviewers. A task binds to one pubkey and cannot be delegated; only the assigned identity submits. An attacker spawning a thousand puppets finds each waiting for a draw that may never come. The reef of tasks is shallow; clones sit idle while the harbor of work narrows. Lucky clones must independently produce work judged by peers. No yarrow stem borrows another mandate. The attacker pays full cost per clone yet harvests from only the few drawn, making rewards sublinear in clone count.
